key_insight: LASP uses an LLM to turn modeling-history semantics into structured B-spline priors, bridging design intent and geometric surface fitting.
engineering_relevance: This can improve CAD surface fitting by providing solver-ready priors that are more semantically consistent than heuristic initialization.
method: Translate procedural modeling histories into rich textual descriptions of intent and geometry.
Fine-tune an LLM to predict structured B-spline prior parameters.
Feed the predicted priors into existing geometric solvers without changing the kernel.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments showing that the language-driven priors improve fitting quality and semantic coherence compared with traditional machine learning schemes.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate history-to-text translation and reliable LLM prior prediction, so errors in semantic extraction could propagate into the solver.
paper_title: Language-Augmented Semantic Priors for B-Spline Surface Fitting
